body: MAINLINE-039 filed, QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. On today's record a rib grid or frame does not buy back gamma at 019's reserve. 028b reproduces exactly; the plain sandwich's best least SF today is 0.528. Record, load-bearing rows read at source: the Isogrid Handbook allows 0.425 only for heavily stiffened domes, from one 1964 aluminium dome; CR-62257's geodesic caps reached 0.57-0.64 while its monocoque caps reached 0.78-0.82; SP-8032 gives stiffened domes the isotropic curve (0.14 at a sphere). SBKF's 0.82-0.98 are cylinders. No framed-sphere test found in sources opened. Concepts: SR-200 tee ribs at 0.5, 1.0 and 2.04 m; 026's s 2.04 m frame in SiC and in Be tubes. Least SF today: ribs 0.517-0.586 (0.586 needs 2.2 t of ribs on the handbook's 0.425, with faces 0.75 and seam 0.65); frames 0.512. Least named set: with 028b's seam screen, none for any stiffened version (plain: gamma x2.82, Q x1.32). At 028b's two values each costs 88-257 kg of reserve or payload. Trade: a Be frame stiff enough to make the 2 m bays clamped caps (0.6-0.8 t, SP-8032 curve about 0.6, named optimism O5) lifts today's least SF to 0.689 and cuts the shortfall to SF 1 from 2.80 t to 1.33 t; ribs at 1 m cut it to 2.42 t. None floats. Grounding: that bay knockdown is a one-bay test, cheaper than a sandwich sphere at Vc 0.95, but still leaves 1.3 t, the seam, Q and r/t-300 tubes. 16 NFI rows. Next: none; the robotics seat sends the next job.
